key_insight: Lone-pair-driven lattice softness in the hybrid perovskite GuaPbI3 creates an ultralow thermal-conductivity solid while still retaining electronically accessible transport pathways.
engineering_relevance: This provides a materials-design route for improving thermoelectric cooling efficiency by suppressing heat flow without fully sacrificing charge transport.
method: Used physics-guided symbolic regression to identify a lone-pair-dominated compositional regime.
Selected GuaPbI3 as a candidate and synthesized it mechanochemically.
Combined thermal/electrical measurements, impedance spectroscopy, and DFT to link structure, phonons, and transport.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an ultralow room-temperature thermal conductivity of 0.088 W m^-1 K^-1, with bias-dependent bulk conduction and bulk-dominated impedance response.
watch_item: The material’s charge transport appears sensitive to bias and chemical potential, so practical device performance may depend strongly on processing, stability, and operating conditions.
paper_title: Lone-Pair-Induced Lattice Softness Enables Ultralow Thermal Conductivity in Hybrid Organic-Inorganic Perovskite GuaPbI$_3$
